newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: PT valued at 1.1-1.5 trillion escudos. [CORRECTED 15:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: PT valued at 1.1-1.5 trillion escudos. [CORRECTED 15:20 GMT]

text.p: Portugal Telecom, due to be partially privatised later this year, has been valued at between 1.1 and 1.5 trillion escudos, Under-Secretary for Communications, Leonor Coutinho, said.

Coutinho said a consortium comprising Banco Portugues de Investimento, Schroders and Lehman Bros had valued PT at 1.1 trillion (corrects figure from 1.5 billion) escudos and another incorporating Banco Essi, UBS, SBC Warburg and Merrill Lynch valued it at 1.1 billion escudos.

A spokesman for the latter consortium said that it had valued PT at between 1.1 and 1.37 trillion escudos. He told Reuters the valuation was carried out in early May when PT's share price was between 6,400 and 6,600 escudos per share.
The valuations were submitted to the Public Works Ministry as part of preparations for the third stage privatisation of 26 percent of the capital of PT, expected in the last quarter 1997.
The Portuguese government will retain a 25 percent "golden share" after the privatisation.
PT shares stood at 7,260 escudos, up 68, in volume of 848,126 on Lisbon bourse at 1140 GMT.
